page:
## Real gear, captured

A capture is a neural network trained to sound like one piece of gear: an amp head, a pedal, or a whole rig from pedal to microphone. CRBN Rig plays Neural Amp Modeler captures (`.nam` files), so the thousands shared on TONE3000 by players and studios are yours to try. Find one you like, drop it in, and play.

## Choosing and customising your own skins

CRBN Rig opens in **CRBN**: carbon fibre cut with a honeycomb, with current running in behind it every time you pick a note. Twenty skins wait in the look menu, under Rig's hardware: ten classic skins after the amps players know, and ten energy skins, CRBN among them, whose light inside the amp answers your playing.

**Salvage** is made from photographs of real scrap metal, cut fresh for your amp, its cabinet and its name plate, so no two rigs look alike. Choose the sheet of old paint and rust, the grille (expanded metal, chicken wire, woven wire or perforated sheet), the grille's metal, the glow behind it and how the words are put on, or press Shuffle for a new cut.

**Build your own** in the Rig builder: take an energy skin's parts (its energy, cutouts, mesh, faceplate, knobs and colour), name your skin, and keep it beside the twenty. Share it as a code that anyone can open in CRBN Rig. Draw your own knobs and switches too: save a template, draw over it in any art app, and bring it back in. Your own art stays on your computer for now; the code shares the rest of the skin.

## Your library

Point CRBN Rig at the folder where you keep your captures and cabinet IRs (your TONE3000 downloads, say). It lists every `.nam` and `.wav` file with what the file says about itself: its name, the gear, the maker and model, the tone and who captured it. Search as you type, filter by gear and tone, sort, and click to play. Star the ones you love. Your folder is there again next time, and the desktop app sees new files as you add them.

## Favourites on standby

Your first ten starred captures wait on keys 1 to 0, loaded and warm, so a switch is a quick fade with no gap. The arrow keys step through them, and the key left of 1 takes you back to the one before. Show them as footswitches, keycaps or a setlist.

## Pedals, rigs and variants

Drag a capture from your library onto the board and it becomes a pedal before the amp: up to four, each with Drive, Level and a Tone you can switch in or bypass, stomped on and off with a fade. Move them along the board by their grips.

Save the whole setup as a rig, by name: the amp's capture, the cabinet, the gate, the EQ, the output level and the board. Every rig has three variants on Q, W and E (Clean, Push and Lead to start), each remembering which pedals are on and how their knobs are set. Export a rig as a small file to keep or share: it names the captures it uses, and never carries the captures themselves.

## Your footswitches

Open the MIDI dock, drag a control onto it (a knob, a switch, a pedal's footswitch, a favourite, a variant or a rig) and press the footswitch or move the pedal you want for it. Switches toggle, or work only while held. An expression pedal can sweep any part of a knob's range, and CRBN Rig measures your pedal's real sweep from heel to toe: rock it five times, or set each end with a click. Program Changes pick variants and rigs. Your controller is named as its box is, once, with no ports to choose.

## Protection

The squeal guard listens for feedback and mutes it within a fraction of a second, and auto-off mutes the amp when a jack is pulled or the input goes dead. A banner says what happened, in words, and Space turns the sound back on. Both are on from the start, with their switches under Protection. Space also puts the amp on standby and back.

## Your chain

- **Input** with its own level, and a meter that tells you when your interface clips.
- **Noise gate** to keep high-gain captures quiet between notes.
- **Pedals**: up to four captures before the amp.
- **The capture**, resampled for you when it was recorded at another rate.
- **EQ**: bass, middle and treble.
- **Cabinet**: a speaker cabinet impulse response (`.wav`).
- **Output**: raw, normalized so every capture sits at about the same loudness, or calibrated to your interface's levels.

## Made for playing

CRBN Rig runs as its own app with your audio interface, through ASIO for the lowest latency, or DirectSound. Pick your input, output, buffer size and sample rate in Audio settings. If you were playing when you closed it, it plays your guitar again as soon as it opens.

## The web version

Open CRBN Rig in your browser from this page: the same chain, library, pedals, rigs and MIDI, nothing to install. Play your guitar through your browser's audio input, or hear the demo riff. Your browser asks once before CRBN Rig can read your folder or your MIDI controller, and nothing you load is uploaded. A browser adds some latency, so the desktop app is the place for serious playing. To play your guitar or use MIDI through it, open it in a browser tab: Pavillion Hub's own window cannot use your audio input or MIDI yet.

## Part of the CRBN suite

CRBN Rig is installed and kept up to date by Pavillion Hub, beside the rest of the CRBN tools.

## Credits

Based on Neural Amp Modeler by Steven Atkinson. Captures and impulse responses belong to their authors.
